# Native linked credential factory, 2026-10-04

The default linked credential factory previously captured whichever descriptors existed on the exported `PgCredentialAuthority.prototype` at its first call. A `ready` accessor installed before that call could be recorded as original and later invoked by the dedicated native read. Existing origin controls mutated methods after registration, so they did not cover that first-selection window. This source finding does not establish an unauthorized native-row mutation or provider call.

This separate three-path correction starts from exact clean `09301572a58a1418a8c576d98eb02d440595065c`. The module captures its original class prototype, parent and data-method descriptors immediately after the class declaration, before the default factory is available. The factory compares that private baseline before construction and registration; origin lookup repeats it before native reads. Replacement methods, accessors, added descriptors or a changed parent cannot become the default origin. No public registrar, supplied constructor or caller attestation is introduced.

The default authority selector is read through its own data descriptor. A recognized cached authority must retain its original provenance. Client selector accessors are refused before the default factory, native read or recognized authority readiness invokes the client callback. Ordinary tooling constructors keep their readiness/API behavior and remain outside default factory membership. Privilege, principal, grant scope, native nonsecret tuple, current membership, approval, source recipe, saved-plan custody and final dispatch predicates are unchanged.

All fifty existing origin identities, callback bodies, selectors, flags and native prerequisites remain exact. Eleven additional controls cover pre-selection `ready`, `getCredential` and `listCredentials` method/accessor replacements, prototype-parent replacement, authority/client selector accessors, cached readiness/client getter refusal and genuine tooling readiness without default origin. Refusal controls require zero hostile callbacks and no new default authority registration; after exact restoration they read the genuine current native tuple. These are physical PostgreSQL/default-factory contract tests with modeled already authenticated principals and synthetic fixture credential hashes. They prove no browser token issuance, hosted transport, effective provider permission or end-to-end worker dispatch.

The existing required flag is `ZENITH_TEST_NATIVE_INTEGRATION_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED=1`, with `ZENITH_TEST_PLATFORM_PG_URL` naming the disposable native owner and an explicit port. The final case contract separately binds the original fifty and eleven added identities; canonical registration is a follow-up owned by the gate author. No missing backend may substitute PGlite or skip mandatory scenarios.

Author imports, compiler, lint, tests, database/Docker/Temporal services, cloud calls, installation and commits are unrun. C/root must independently review the frozen three-path source, then root runs pinned compiler/lint and all 61 native origin scenarios plus the original 172 current-dispatch/source controls. The separate corrected OAuth dispatch packet and its native execution remain independent. Historical source receipts and runtime failures stay unchanged.

This private module baseline assumes module initialization and standard runtime primitives have not already been replaced. It prevents post-initialization, pre-first-factory descriptor mutation; it does not certify arbitrary module-loader or process-wide prototype integrity. Hot reload/cached historical instances without this module's private registry remain refused until a trusted fresh process selects the default owner.
